concepts.def: The 1920s economic boom driven by mass production, consumer goods, advertising and credit, although farmers, Black Americans and older industries largely missed out.
The ban on making and selling alcohol under the 18th Amendment from 1920, which fuelled speakeasies, bootlegging and organised crime until repeal in 1933.
Assembly-line manufacturing pioneered by Henry Ford with the Model T, cutting costs so ordinary families could afford cars and consumer goods.
The collapse of share prices in October 1929 that wiped out investors, triggered bank failures and helped tip the USA into the Great Depression.
The severe economic slump after 1929: by 1933 around a quarter of the workforce was unemployed and shanty towns nicknamed 'Hoovervilles' spread.
Franklin D. Roosevelt's programme of relief, recovery and reform from 1933, using 'alphabet agencies' such as the CCC and TVA to fight the Depression.

mcqs.q: Which constitutional amendment introduced Prohibition in 1920?
options: The 18th Amendment
The 19th Amendment
The 21st Amendment
The 16th Amendment
A shanty town built by homeless people during the Depression, named mockingly after President Hoover
A New Deal agency that built dams
An illegal bar selling alcohol during Prohibition
A government-built suburb of the 1920s

mcqs.q: Which president launched the New Deal in 1933?
options: Herbert Hoover
Calvin Coolidge
Franklin D. Roosevelt
Woodrow Wilson

mcqs.q: Why did many American farmers struggle during the 1920s boom?
options: Overproduction and falling crop prices left many farmers in debt while demand declined
Prohibition made it illegal to grow grain
The New Deal taxed farms heavily
All farmland was destroyed by the Dust Bowl during the 1920s

mcqs.q: Did Prohibition stop Americans drinking alcohol?
options: The Depression was caused by American spending on the Second World War.
Prohibition successfully eliminated drinking in America until it was repealed in 1933.
Prohibition only banned drinking in public parks.
No — drinking continued in illegal speakeasies supplied by bootleggers, and organised crime figures such as Al Capone grew rich on the trade.
The 1929 Crash alone instantly caused the whole Depression.
The Wall Street Crash exposed deeper weaknesses — overproduction, unequal wealth, weak banks and shrinking demand — which combined to produce a prolonged slump.
The New Deal abolished the US dollar to fight the Depression.
The Depression was caused by American spending on the Second World War.

mcqs.q: Did the New Deal end the Great Depression?
options: The New Deal completely ended the Depression within Roosevelt's first term.
The New Deal abolished the US dollar to fight the Depression.
It cut unemployment, restored confidence in banks and provided relief, but recovery was incomplete — full employment only returned with rearmament and the Second World War.
The Depression was caused by American spending on the Second World War.
